headline: Steam replaces chemicals as California strawberry yields soar
meta_description: California farmer Rod Koda nearly doubled his organic strawberry harvest using steam treatment instead of chemical fumigants in fields.
summary_short: California strawberry farmer Rod Koda nearly doubled his organic harvest by switching from chemical fumigants to steam treatment in his fields.
body:
California strawberry farmer Rod Koda nearly doubled his organic strawberry harvest in fields treated with steam instead of chemical fumigants.

The shift represents a significant breakthrough for sustainable farming. Rather than relying on traditional chemical treatments to prepare soil, Koda's fields received steam application—a method that appears to dramatically boost yields while keeping crops certified organic.

Researchers are now working to develop the technology further, hoping to make steam treatment more accessible and practical for other farmers. The success in Koda's fields suggests a promising path forward: higher harvests, cleaner land, and a reduced reliance on synthetic chemicals. As organic farming grows in demand, innovations like this could help growers meet market needs without compromising their environmental principles.

Researchers developing the technology for broader farm adoption
